title: Tadla irrigated plain, Beni Moussa side, 2 Sep to 14 Sep 2026
summary: From 2 Sep to 14 Sep 2026 the radar shows 2.37 km2 turning brighter and 1.31 km2 darker in HV on the Tadla plain, inside the 9 km circle. Most of the brighter area, 1.32 km2, is on the changing fields.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 12 days mean HV moved by 0.01 dB and mean HH by 0.0 dB. In HV, 2.37 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 1.31 km2 darker; in HH, 5.77 km2 turned brighter and 1.98 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields had 1.32 km2 brighter and 0.38 km2 darker in HV, with a mean HV change of 0.31 dB. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.68 km2 brighter and 0.6 km2 darker in HV. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes changed by -0.04 dB in HV, and built-up land by -0.12 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the brighter fields: new crops sown after the summer harvest, which add volume scattering; sowing records or a field visit would confirm it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. One track only, so field edges facing away from the radar can look darker. Small patches are close to what speckle alone can produce at the 3 dB threshold.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: An irrigation office could compare the 1.32 km2 of brighter fields with its sowing and water-delivery records, since these plots are growing a crop now.
